pure-announcement.rationale: The note explains the platform's mechanisms — snapshot-backed microVMs, on-demand image loading, memory ballooning — rather than announcing a launch or release.

duplicate.rationale: The closest concept is a W2S research sandbox; none of the nearest concepts covers scale-out microVM infrastructure for agent environments.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The production claims are tied to the linked Kimi K3 tech report and the open-source implementation itself.

durability.rationale: The design trade-offs — sub-100ms snapshot/fork of Firecracker environments, local disk as a bounded cache over on-demand OCI images, and ballooning to reclaim idle-environment memory — are systems patterns for agent sandboxing that will outlast the specific 9.6x and 1.5M-image figures.

actionability.rationale: It changes how someone would build agent-RL or sandbox infrastructure — pause and fork environments instead of keeping them warm — and the E2B-compatible API gives an immediate adoption path without code changes.

atomicity.rationale: Everything in the note serves one idea — running agent environments at scale on snapshot-backed microVMs — with the CLI reference and install steps as packaging around it.
